newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares expected to catch up on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares expected to catch up on Thursday.

text.p: The Bel-20 index, weighed down Wednesday due to caution and profit-taking ahead of the release of first-half earnings by index heavyweights, is expected to easily make up for the dip on Thursday, dealers said.
The Bel-20 ended 0.13 percent lower at 2,596.36 despite a confident start on Wall Street and stronger bonds.
"All the elements are fine, there is no reason why we should't advance tomorrow," one dealer said.
Players held back mainly due to the release of H1 results from chemicals and drugs firm UCB after the close on Wednesday and from chemicals firm Solvay Thursday.
UCB announced after the close of business that H1 ordinary profit was up 33 percent at 3.89 billion francs, which was in line with analysts' expectations who had put forward a 30 to 35 percent rise.

One dealer said that UCB was already very expensive and that the market was expecting at least a 35 percent rise for it to rise further. "Between 30 and 35 (percent) the market will not be euphoric," he said.
UCB began to take off at the end of May, when it was at 95,600 francs, peaking at 153,000 on July 17. It closed down 0.5 percent at 139,250 francs before the earnings release.
Solvay was a notable loser with its 1.8 percent drop to 23,450 francs.

Players took profit after becoming increasingly pessimistic about Solvay's earnings announcement in the wake of first-half earnings of Dutch chemicals group DSM NV earlier on Wednesday which were at the lower-end of market expectations.

"People are getting out (of Solvay) because they are not all too positive about the results," one trader said. Another said a major London brokerage had announced Solvay would not meet its profit target. DSM itself was hammered in Amsterdam, closing eight percent lower at 211.50 guilders.
Kredietbank ended 2.2 percent stronger on renewed talk of merger plans with another Belgian bank, Cera, as a precursor to cooperation with Dutch Rabobank.

"(KB and Cera) are no longer denying the reports," one trader said. He said the market was expecting a full merger or close cooperation between the two Belgian banks. There were doubts however about a partnership with Rabobank, he added.

One trader said the rumours of a deal with Cera, which erupted early June, had been virtually discounted in KB's share price and that upward potential was limited. "On the contrary, (KB) will slide if it would be called off," he said.
KB was still at 14,850 francs when first reports of talks with Cera and Rabobank emerged.
Belgian financial daily L'Echo quoted the chairman of Belgian holding company Almanij, Jan Huyghebaert, as saying there was a certain logic to an alliance with Cera.
Almanij, KB's main shareholder, gained 0.7 percent to 17,100 francs.
